findings.title: Necessary reductions are not global FFT results
findings.finding: The onion reductions, dual equations, spectral minors and two-defect tail are open-chart constraints or identities. They do not solve the residual equations, construct a complete factorization, establish an asymptotic transform cost, or prove global impossibility.

findings.title: Omitted strata remain mathematically live
findings.finding: Denominator clearing and rational reconstruction require nonzero guards; S1=0 is demonstrably compatible with invertible partial candidates in exception_s1.py. Exceptional linear systems need their own consistency/family analysis. alpha=0 is a separately justified singular-column exclusion. Do not convert chart exclusions into general exclusions.

findings.title: Anchored-minor success needs corner guards
findings.finding: Thirty anchored minors vanish identically for some matrices outside quasiseparable order one when anchors vanish. independent_gf17_audit counts full_B_success before testing B/A corners. Its observed zero-success result is safe as an exclusion of a superset; a future positive flag would need a stronger validator.

findings.title: Resultants and Jacobian rank have limited implications
findings.finding: Three resultants based on a zero reference pencil can vanish without a common solution. A nonzero modular Jacobian minor establishes specialized polynomial independence; lifting needs authenticated exact reductions. It does not prove a regular common-zero locus, infeasibility, or feasible FFT parameters.

findings.title: Some verifiers permit vacuous sample success
findings.finding: general_onion.verify, onion_peel.mod_check, dual_sparse_polynomials.modular_validation and upper_minor.verify skip singular samples without a built-in minimum. Some companion tests restore minimum counts, but test_new_gate.test_modular_upper_residuals checks only nonzero resultants and ignores verified count.

findings.title: GF(17) exclusion must retain all qualifications
findings.finding: The saved exhaustive result concerns p=17, root 9, one permutation, and the regular rational chart only. It covers neither extension fields, other roots/permutations, characteristic zero nor omitted strata. Fresh data integrity confirms preserved records, not a rerun or independent residual recomputation.

findings.title: ZIP CRC and log strings are not authenticated regression certificates
findings.finding: Both recursive runners execute unpacked checkpoint programs after CRC checks without pinned cryptographic identities and rely in part on transcript substrings. build_archive is metadata-dependent despite its reproducible-ZIP wording.

findings.title: The implementations remain dense and domain-bounded
findings.finding: Public arithmetic helpers do not generally validate prime/root assumptions. Dense n×n matrix products and rank/inversion dominate chart tests. int64 modular products need explicit size bounds; the supplied small constants are safe under elementary bounds, but arbitrary p/n are not.

findings.title: No supplied source was executed and assert-based acceptance is conditional
findings.finding: This review is inert static reading plus data integrity. Any saved run claims are historical. Import side effects in build_archive/export_onion_spec and recursive subprocess runners reinforce why source was not imported. python -O can remove critical assert-based validations.

findings.title: One of fifteen exact hashes is already fully covered
findings.finding: inverse_quartic.py hash d9276635d8747ad1eb2c41d6e829f1901d1adeb2dffec15dc71672139ac970c4 was already reviewed in inverse_gate_batch3_review_0313 and the additive registry. Only fourteen hashes add coverage.

per_source.title: General eight-coordinate open chart
per_source.mathematical_scope: Builds a separated-generator, diagonal-one C and B=F C[:,perm] modulo p. Four anchored families are eliminated; the remaining (n−4)(n−5) identities are explicitly not solved. For n=8 the reduction is 30→12 equations. For n=64 it leaves 3,540 identities. The eight coordinates describe the guarded patch, not a complete parameterization of every possible FFT factorization.
per_source.guards_and_acceptance: Lines 18–20 assert n≥6, eight coordinates, a true permutation with prefix (n−1,0,n−2). Lines 22–26 invert z, t, h0 and z−1. Every S1[k], the boundary determinant, every interior Delta and alpha must be nonzero (42–66). alpha=0 is rejected as a singular column pair. The returned denominator list omits z−1 and alpha; alpha is a separate field. Primality of p and exact root order are caller preconditions, not validated by build. Det(C), B corner anchors and inverse-A corners are not acceptance guards in build.
per_source.tests_and_certificate_limits: verify (84–114) samples nonzero coordinates, skips ZeroDivisionError without replenishment, counts C rank and B anchors, and checks coordinate recovery only when both B anchors are nonzero. Its main mode has no minimum valid-sample assertion. The companion unittest does demand four valid, full-rank, B-anchored samples. Assertions are Python assert and disappear with optimization.
per_source.cost_and_implementation: O(n²) scalar construction/prefix-tail sums and dense storage; dense F@C and rank checks are O(n³). NumPy int64 modular reduction occurs after products/sums; require an overflow bound such as n(p−1)²≤2^63−1, plus elimination bounds. Supplied n≤64 and p≤65537 lie safely below those elementary bounds, but the public generic API does not enforce them.

per_source.title: Modular Jacobian independence witness
per_source.mathematical_scope: Forms a quartic lower condition and three upper resultants in eight variables, then seeks a nonzero 4×4 Jacobian minor over GF(p). This is evidence for algebraic independence of the specialized four polynomials. Lifting to Q(zeta8), as the returned status claims, also requires that these are verified reductions of the intended exact characteristic-zero polynomials at an admissible prime/root.
per_source.guards_and_acceptance: The default root is supplied by primitive_root(p,8); a caller-provided root and prime are not checked. There are no chart-denominator or equation-zero checks on the random witness point. Those are unnecessary for polynomial independence, but mean the point is not a feasible factorization witness or a smooth point on the common zero set.
per_source.tests_and_certificate_limits: Lines 23–38 require rank four twice, recompute a pivot determinant, and assert it is nonzero. At most trials random points and up to binomial(8,4)=70 column sets are examined; failure raises ValueError. The regression checks a deterministic minor value and selected columns, not a standalone externally supplied certificate validator.
per_source.cost_and_implementation: Fixed n=8 polynomial construction dominates; Jacobian evaluation scales with generated monomial counts. Numeric row reduction uses int64 and inherits prime-size overflow restrictions. Algebraic independence neither proves the four-equation zero locus has codimension four everywhere nor proves any infeasibility.

per_source.title: Inverse quartic model, previously covered exact hash
per_source.mathematical_scope: Exact sparse arithmetic over Z[z]/(z^4+1) generates 30 degree-at-most-four anchored B identities for the diagonal-one, normalized inverse-stage chart with 26 parameters. The header correctly calls this a feasibility formulation, not an FFT exclusion certificate.
per_source.guards_and_acceptance: Corner anchoring and diagonal normalization are chart assumptions. eq_entries/identities impose minors but do not enforce nonzero anchors or invertibility. root8 checks divisibility and an eighth-root condition but not primality. Modular inversion and rank routines use int64.
per_source.tests_and_certificate_limits: The source was reread in full, including synthetic factorization tests, complementary-cut ranks, exact quotient coefficient evaluation, and export hashing. It already has full first-to-last coverage in inverse_gate_batch3_review_0313/COVERAGE.json and ADDITIVE_CODE_COVERAGE.json. It receives zero new coverage credit here.
per_source.cost_and_implementation: Sparse symbolic products cost products of term counts; modular inversion/rank and matrix multiplication are cubic in matrix dimension. No supplied tests were run during this review.

per_source.title: Archive and manifest builder
per_source.mathematical_scope: Packages all immediate regular files except the existing SHA256SUMS.txt; generates a new manifest and a ZIP in the parent directory. This is distribution plumbing, with no mathematical certificate acceptance.
per_source.guards_and_acceptance: No entrypoint guard: importing this file would write/replace the manifest and archive. Immediate file enumeration is not an allowlist and does not recursively include directories. Existing source files are only read if run; this review did not run it.
per_source.tests_and_certificate_limits: CRC testing and archive member count are asserted, but no post-build verification ties each archived byte string to its manifest digest. The advertised “reproducible” ZIP is not byte-reproducible across metadata changes: zipfile.write preserves timestamps and platform metadata, and the generated manifest has a fresh modification time.
per_source.cost_and_implementation: Work is linear in total input bytes plus compression; read_bytes materializes each file and later the complete archive. SHA256SUMS establishes consistency only when independently trusted; a checksum/CRC does not authenticate code that a runner will execute.

per_source.title: Column-cleared dual-support polynomial system
per_source.mathematical_scope: Constructs 20 residual polynomials in 16 variables over Z[z]/(z^4+1) after ten formal identities vanish. Every B column is cleared by D=t(z−1), with its own S factor where relevant, rather than a global denominator product. construct_dual checks precisely the ten expected zero polynomial names.
per_source.guards_and_acceptance: Cleared equations are equivalent to their rational counterparts only with all clearing denominators nonzero. h0, B anchors, det(C), and inverse corners are additional membership guards listed in export metadata, but not enforced by the exported equation list. No saturation or exceptional-chart enumeration is performed. Zero factors can create extraneous algebraic solutions.
per_source.tests_and_certificate_limits: modular_validation compares all 64 matrix entries and twenty scaled minors using factor_from_dual at two primes and two root variants. It skips failed denominators and does not itself require a positive sample count. test_dual_gate requires twelve accepted samples and exact term equality to the saved equation JSON. The imported factor generator remains a dependency; this batch is not a complete import-closure audit.
per_source.cost_and_implementation: Sparse polynomial multiplication is quadratic in operand term counts; fixed-size symbolic expansion can still grow substantially. Stored tests describe degree nine and 8,437 terms; this review did not regenerate those polynomials. No fast transform is implemented.

per_source.title: An explicitly omitted S1=0 stratum
per_source.mathematical_scope: Searches at most 200 deterministic pseudorandom choices with gamma=1 and h0=1, forcing S1=0 while solving V1 through a different nonzero R1 pivot. Returns an invertible C, B anchors and inverse-A anchors satisfying the first ten support identities but failing at least one remaining identity.
per_source.guards_and_acceptance: Other S values, the replacement R pivot, C full rank, B corners and inverse-A corners are checked. The deliberately free eta1=7 is fixed for the supplied primes. This is a witness in an omitted partial-feasibility stratum, not a full Fourier factorization, and says nothing about all such strata.
per_source.tests_and_certificate_limits: The function asserts at least one residual remains nonzero; the regression expects all twenty residuals nonzero for its two selected primes. Finite-field witnesses are not characteristic-zero existence witnesses. The source does establish why silently dropping the S1=0 branch cannot be advertised as a global search.
per_source.cost_and_implementation: At most 200 fixed-size dense builds, rank checks and inversions, with a failure if no witness is found. NumPy modular arithmetic retains the same bounded-prime restriction.

per_source.title: Twelve-equation specification exporter
per_source.mathematical_scope: Writes equation names, generic anchored-minor formulae, a pointer to the rational evaluator and proof, and one deliberate nonsolution at p=12289. It is metadata plus an evaluation record, not a serialized set of exact expanded rational functions or an independently checkable characteristic-zero certificate.
per_source.guards_and_acceptance: The scope string explicitly requires det(C), B anchors, inverse-A corners and nonzero denominators. These are not all checked by this exporter; it only obtains build outputs and records rank(C). Its fixed point has all twelve residuals asserted nonzero.
per_source.tests_and_certificate_limits: The module has no entrypoint guard, so an import would build matrices and write JSON. Assertions establish exactly twelve residual names and nonzero sampled values only. The linked PROOF_CERTIFICATE.md is an external dependency, not proven by naming it.
per_source.cost_and_implementation: A single fixed-n build plus rank calculation and serialization. Its file hash is a preservation identity; it is not evidence that the equations have no roots.

per_source.title: Earlier n=8 onion reconstruction
per_source.mathematical_scope: Specializes the same eight-coordinate reduction to n=8; the three-mode head recurrence, 2×2 boundary system and interior two-row systems eliminate eighteen rank identities, leaving twelve. The docstring correctly disclaims finding a Fourier factorization.
per_source.guards_and_acceptance: Checks t,h0,z−1,S1, boundary determinant, Deltas and alpha. The passed permutation is not explicitly validated for length, bijection or required prefix. Matrix indexing or the later asserts may catch bad inputs, but there is no standalone parameter-domain validator. No C invertibility or corner acceptance is required by build_onion itself.
per_source.tests_and_certificate_limits: mod_check skips denominator failures, requires every valid random sample to have some remaining nonzero residual, and checks the H recurrence. It has no lower bound on accepted sample count, so zero successful samples can return status metadata. The paired reconstruction regression compares this routine to general_onion, which shares essentially the same formulae; agreement is useful regression evidence, not independent derivation.
per_source.cost_and_implementation: Fixed-size dense matrix construction; symbolic exactness over characteristic zero depends on an external derivation, not finite samples. The returned nonzero-denominator list omits z−1 and records alpha separately.

per_source.title: Earlier nested regression runner
per_source.mathematical_scope: Runs test_dual_gate.py, extracts the prior ZIP to a temporary directory, then runs its run_all.py. A successful return prints 55/55 as 8 new plus 47 previous tests.
per_source.guards_and_acceptance: Execution is intentionally outside this static review. CRC is checked, but the checkpoint is not authenticated against a pinned digest before launching its program. The child environment and dependencies are inherited, stdout/stderr are buffered, and no timeout/resource bound is set.
per_source.tests_and_certificate_limits: Nonzero process exit propagates. The numerical claim additionally trusts two transcript substrings rather than structured individual test results. ZIP CRC plus existence of expected paths does not establish that the executable checkpoint is the intended audited version.
per_source.cost_and_implementation: Cost is the recursive prior test suite plus extraction and memory for captured logs; test count is not a mathematical acceptance criterion. A modified runner could print the expected string, so these strings are not standalone certificate evidence.

per_source.title: Eight dual-support/onion regression tests
per_source.mathematical_scope: Reads the complete eight-test suite: n8/n16 dual support, exact twenty-equation serialization, modular polynomial/matrix agreement, n8/n16/n32/n64 chart checks, paired reconstruction, generic inverse chart checks, S1 exceptional witnesses and prior ZIP checks.
per_source.guards_and_acceptance: The suite usefully demands exact accepted-sample counts, full rank and nonzero B anchors for several deterministic cases. It does not test primality/root misuse, arbitrary permutations, overflow limits, all singular reconstruction branches or adversarial acceptance of zero-anchor candidates.
per_source.tests_and_certificate_limits: The saved polynomial JSON is compared term-for-term against generated equations, a strong regression check for those exact bytes. Its prior-ZIP preservation test checks CRC and one filename, not a pinned cryptographic hash. Many “independent” checks call the same helper modules or duplicate formulae. No tests are run here.
per_source.cost_and_implementation: Symbolic equation expansion and dense n=64 inversion dominate the designed workload. Assertions inside the helpers can vanish under Python optimization even though unittest assertion methods remain active.

per_source.title: Spectral regression and finite-field runner
per_source.mathematical_scope: Runs nine new tests and a freshly extracted prior runner, expecting the 55-test transcript, then calls exhaust_smallfield.go(17) and compares eight aggregate counts. It prints a 64/64 plus GF(17) reproduction message.
per_source.guards_and_acceptance: No pinned checkpoint digest is checked before prior code execution. The GF(17) helper and expected JSON are imported/read from the current source directory and share its trust boundary. The runner validates selected counts, not the full candidate set, every guard counter, root/permutation metadata or a characteristic-zero proof.
per_source.tests_and_certificate_limits: Exit codes and the “Ran 9 tests”/“OK” strings are checked, as are h_checked, tail exceptions, t_zero, lower survivors, upper gamma pairs, reconstruction exceptions, invertible candidates and full_B_success. None of this was rerun by the current review. The returned new/old logs do not themselves include an independent certificate validator.
per_source.cost_and_implementation: Includes the complete nested prior workload and a finite exhaustive enumeration; captured subprocess logs can grow without a bound. No timeout is set.

per_source.title: Nine spectral determinant regression tests
per_source.mathematical_scope: Checks exact quartic/resultant sizes, modular quartic agreement, nonzero upper resultants, one deterministic Jacobian witness, one five-parameter value, one adjacent-tail cubic, randomized Vandermonde rank equivalence and the two-defect tail identity.
per_source.guards_and_acceptance: These are finite or structural regression checks for necessary gates, not factorization acceptance. They do not cover discarded rational strata or prove that the nonlinear system is infeasible. Imported exact construction and gate helpers are outside this batch except where separately listed.
per_source.tests_and_certificate_limits: Concrete gap at lines 55–59: verify_upper can return verified=0, but the test only requires its three elimination polynomials to be nonzero. It never asserts any sampled direct-vs-symbolic upper determinant comparison occurred. In contrast, the quartic test requires at least five accepted samples and the two-defect test requires >2,000 checked rows.
per_source.cost_and_implementation: rank_rect is fresh list-based modular elimination, so those small rank checks avoid NumPy int64 overflow, but the imported routines may not. Source test counts and expected constants are reviewed, not freshly executed or regenerated.

per_source.title: Two-defect Fourier-tail identity checker
per_source.mathematical_scope: After the three-mode head recurrence, the first B column for i≥3 is the sum of two explicit defect characters: (h[n−2]−hstar[n−2])z^(−2i)+(1−hstar[n−1])z^(−i). The header correctly says this is a support statement, not a cost improvement.
per_source.guards_and_acceptance: Relies on general_onion.build and the special permutation prefix. Rational reconstruction failures are skipped, so this remains an open-chart statement. It does not check that remaining B minors vanish or that a full stage factorization is feasible.
per_source.tests_and_certificate_limits: Tests twelve seeded attempts for each n in {8,16,32,64} and p in {12289,65537}, checks every tail row for accepted samples, and explicitly requires at least seven accepted samples in each group. This avoids the zero-sample weakness found in upper_minor.verify.
per_source.cost_and_implementation: The identity formula takes O(n) work per sample, but the current checker constructs dense F and C and multiplies them through build, costing O(n³). A short formula for one tail is not an end-to-end FFT algorithm or bound.

per_source.title: Necessary row-three upper minors and resultants
per_source.mathematical_scope: Builds four 3×3 determinant pencils a_k−gamma3*b_k for k=4,1,2,5 and eliminates gamma3 using three resultants against k=4. These are necessary conditions. The source correctly disclaims sufficiency and generic FFT impossibility.
per_source.guards_and_acceptance: A zero reference pencil (a4,b4)=(0,0) makes all three stored pairwise resultants vanish regardless of the other pencils. More generally, elimination does not restore reconstruction guards or ensure a common gamma3 on degenerate leading-coefficient strata. Primitive eighth-root order and prime assumptions are not enforced by generate.
per_source.tests_and_certificate_limits: verify compares each scaled symbolic determinant with a direct determinant for accepted random chart points. Denominator failures are skipped with no positive-count requirement. Returned “nonzero” flags only mean the resultant polynomial is not identically zero, not that sampled residuals vanish, no solutions exist, or tests actually ran.
per_source.cost_and_implementation: Fixed-size sparse symbolic ring arithmetic in eight variables dominates; resultant products scale with polynomial term counts. The unused det4 import still introduces a dependency. build and polynomial construction share inputs/formulae, so this is a consistency check rather than a full independent proof.

per_source.title: Independent fixed-chart GF(17) enumeration audit
per_source.mathematical_scope: Pure-standard-library audit specialized to p=17, z=9, n=8 and one fixed permutation. It independently interpolates head/tail modes, solves the two tail equations for t,beta, compares lower determinant and upper coefficient data, enumerates all 17² gamma pairs for surviving head tuples, reconstructs via generic linear solves, checks all thirty B minors and direct F=BPA for invertible C.
per_source.guards_and_acceptance: Explicitly excludes h0=0, singular tail 2×2 systems, t=0, zero S1 values, singular boundary systems and interior Deltas. alpha=0 is additionally proved to give proportional columns. Thus it is exhaustive only for this guarded finite-field chart. Full B-minor success is counted at 247–248 before B/A corner guards are inspected at 250–256; the success flag would not alone certify separated-factor membership on zero-anchor cases. For the saved zero-success result, this larger acceptance set makes the exclusion conservative.
per_source.tests_and_certificate_limits: Saved comparison targets are data, not imported programs. Exact count equality, 2,546 certificate count, zero successes, first eight examples, direct inverse/product checks and endpoint formula checks are asserted. All acceptance assertions disappear with python -O; the result can still write positive verification flags without enforcement. There is no CLI optimization guard or external trusted input digest check. This review ran no supplied code. Fresh data-only checks confirm 2,546 saved records, thirty residuals each, a nonzero residual in each, nonzero stored det(C), and the saved certificate digest match; they do not recompute residuals.
per_source.cost_and_implementation: Enumerates 17^4=83,521 h tuples (78,608 with h0≠0), then up to 17² gamma pairs per survivor: a naive field-size generalization is O(p^6) fixed-matrix work and candidate storage. Saved data records 4,596 lower survivors and 1,328,244 gamma pairs. It is not an asymptotically faster Fourier transform. Pure Python integers avoid the NumPy overflow concern.
